question: Relapse to smoking after a cessation attempt is primarily a sign of weak willpower and moral failure, rather than reflecting the pharmacological and psychosocial complexity of nicotine dependence.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. Nicotine dependence involves neurobiological addiction (mesolimbic dopamine pathway), physical withdrawal, and powerful psychosocial conditioning. Most smokers make 8–10 attempts before achieving sustained abstinence. Attributing relapse to moral failure is both inaccurate and harmful to the doctor-patient relationship.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Nicotine dependence is a recognised neurobiological disorder (ICD-11 6C4A). Relapse reflects dopaminergic reinforcement, withdrawal symptoms, conditioned cues, and social triggers. Framing it as a willpower failure is clinically incorrect and damages the therapeutic relationship.
